A stale row in the admin UI (host already deleted in another tab) or a forged ID yields an unhandled NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a 404; save_host also does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` which raises ActionController::Parameters missing-key errors for malformed payloads.

If the record doesn’t exist (stale UI row / forged id), `host` is `nil`, causing `NoMethodError` (e.g., `nil.destroy` or `nil.host=` inside `save_host`). Additionally, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without guarding, which can raise on malformed payloads. These are verifiable crash paths in the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The embed_category lookup crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site_setting row is absent or has no matching category, which is the default state for nearly every install. Discourse only writes a site_settings row when an admin has set the setting; on any site that never set embed_category the SELECT returns zero rows, `embeddable_hosts[0]` is nil, and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration mid-deploy so the new code (which reads EmbeddableHost exclusively) has no table at all.
records.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it unconditionally indexes into the SQL result: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If the `site_settings` table has no row for `embed_category` (which is plausible since defaults may not be persisted as rows), `execute(...)[0]` will be `nil` and `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration before the fallback `if category_id == 0` can run.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The data migration guards the row inserts on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`, which is always 0 for a SELECT in PostgreSQL, so the inserts never run while the paired DELETE unconditionally destroys the old settings. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The category backfill joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but Discourse category-type settings store 'name,slug' pairs and category names are not unique across sites with renamed categories, so the target category resolution is lossy. Sites where embed_category was stored in the 'name,slug' form get no join match and silently fall back to uncategorized, re-classifying every migrated host's posting category without any warning.
records.rationale: The migration resolves `embed_category` via a lossy/fragile join on the *current* category name: `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). If that setting value doesn’t exactly match `categories.name` (e.g., different stored format, or the category was renamed), `category_id` becomes 0 and the code silently falls back to `uncategorized_category_id`, causing migrated `embeddable_hosts` rows to be assigned the wrong posting category without warning.

records.issue_text: [BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil record when the id doesn't exist. DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id raises NoMethodError (undefined method `destroy' for nil), returning a raw 500 instead of a 404 the admin API contract implies; the user sees an unhandled error page rather than a meaningful message.
records.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately use the result without a nil check: `save_host(host)` in `update` and `host.destroy` in `destroy`. If the record doesn’t exist (stale UI row / forged id), `host` is `nil`, causing `NoMethodError` (e.g., `nil.destroy` or `nil.host=` inside `save_host`). Additionally, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without guarding, which can raise on malformed payloads. These are verifiable crash paths in the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete action's destroyRecord() promise chain has no .catch, unlike save which uses popupAjaxError. When the DELETE request fails (network error, 500, stale record), the rejection is silently swallowed: no error dialog appears, the row stays in the list, and the admin believes the host was deleted while it still authorizes embeds — a user-facing operation whose failure is invisible.
records.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `save()` action handles failures via `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, but the `delete()` action does not: `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` has no `.catch(...)`. If the DELETE request rejects, there is no error dialog/handler shown in this code path, unlike save, so failures can be invisible to the admin.

After saving, a later edit-then-cancel on the same row calls rollbackBuffer(), which re-renders the row with the pre-save host name/category in the UI while the server holds the new values — the admin sees stale state that disagrees with what's actually enforced until a page reload.
